verses.text: Those who are enslaved should consider their masters worthy of full respect, so God's name and our teaching won't be slandered.

If their masters are believers, they must not disrespect them because they're brothers and sisters. Instead, they should serve them even better, because those who benefit from their work are believers and beloved. Teach and urge these things.
If anyone teaches something different and won't agree with the sound teaching of our Lord Jesus Christ and the godly instruction,
they are conceited and understand nothing. They have an unhealthy craving for arguments and word battles, which produce envy, conflict, insults, evil suspicions,
and constant friction among people whose minds are corrupt and who have lost the truth. They think godliness is a way to make money. Stay away from such people.
Godliness with contentment is great gain.
We brought nothing into the world, and we can't take anything out of it.
So if we have food and clothing, we'll be content with that.
Those who are determined to get rich fall into temptation and a trap, and into many foolish and harmful desires that drag people down into ruin and destruction.
The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some, craving it, have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many pains.
But you, man of God, run from these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, which you were called to and confessed when you made your good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to everything, and Christ Jesus, who made his good confession before Pontius Pilate:
keep this command without stain or blame until our Lord Jesus Christ appears.
At the right time, God will bring about his appearing—God, the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
He alone is immortal and lives in unapproachable light. No one has seen him or can see him. To him be honor and eternal power. Amen.
Tell those who are rich in this present age not to be arrogant or put their hope in wealth, which is uncertain, but in God, who richly gives us everything to enjoy.
Tell them to do good, to be rich in good works, and to be generous and ready to share.
By doing this, they'll store up treasure for themselves as a firm foundation for the future, so they can take hold of the life that is truly life.
Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you. Turn away from pointless chatter and the opposing arguments of what is falsely called knowledge.
Some have claimed this knowledge and wandered away from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.
